meta.name: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A
meta.note: ISO/IEC 27001 is a copyrighted standard. No control text or Annex A title from it is reproduced here. Each entry holds the control identifier, which is a factual reference, and an original subject line written for this site. Consult the standard itself for authoritative wording.

themes.name: Organizational
themes.blurb: The controls that decide how security is governed: who owns it, what the rules are, and how the organization holds itself and its suppliers to them.

themes.name: People
themes.blurb: The controls that address the human side: who is hired, what they agree to, what they are taught, and what happens when they leave.

themes.name: Physical
themes.blurb: The controls that keep people away from equipment and information they should not reach, and protect that equipment from its surroundings.

themes.name: Technological
themes.blurb: The controls implemented in and around the technology itself: endpoints, access, networks, software, and the data moving between them.

controls.subject: Written security policies, approved and kept current
controls.metaphor: Writing the house rules down and pinning them to the fridge, so nobody has to guess.
controls.translation: The family agrees its house rules in writing, the adults sign off on them, and they revisit them when circumstances change rather than letting them go stale.

controls.subject: Named security roles and the authority that comes with them
controls.metaphor: Deciding who is responsible for locking up at night, and telling them so.
controls.translation: The family names who is responsible for each part of keeping the house safe, and gives them the standing to actually make those calls.

controls.subject: Separating duties so no one person can act unchecked
controls.metaphor: One person writes the cheque, another signs it.
controls.translation: The family splits sensitive jobs between people, so that no single member can both make a decision and approve it without anyone noticing.

controls.subject: Management actively backing the security program
controls.metaphor: Parents who follow the house rules themselves, not just enforce them.
controls.translation: The adults visibly back the rules and follow them too, because rules nobody at the top honours are rules nobody else will honour either.

controls.subject: Working relationships with regulators and law enforcement
controls.metaphor: Knowing which neighbour to call, and having the non-emergency police number on the fridge.
controls.translation: The family keeps working relationships with the people they would need in a crisis, so the first call is not the first conversation.

controls.subject: Membership of industry and peer security groups
controls.metaphor: Joining the neighbourhood watch group, so you hear about break-ins nearby.
controls.translation: The family stays connected to groups who share what is happening locally, so they learn about problems from someone else's experience rather than their own.

controls.subject: Gathering and acting on threat intelligence
controls.metaphor: Reading the local notices about a spate of car break-ins, and moving the car into the garage.
controls.translation: The family pays attention to warnings about what is happening nearby and actually changes what it does in response, rather than just noting the news.

controls.subject: Security built into projects from the start
controls.metaphor: Deciding where the locks go while the extension is still on paper, not after it is built.
controls.translation: The family thinks about safety while a project is being planned, because it is far cheaper to design a door properly than to retrofit one later.

controls.subject: Knowing what information and assets exist and who owns them
controls.metaphor: Knowing what is in the house, and who is responsible for each thing.
controls.translation: The family keeps track of what it owns and what information it holds, and each item has someone accountable for looking after it.

controls.subject: Rules for handling assets acceptably
controls.metaphor: Agreeing that the good camera can be borrowed, but not taken to the beach.
controls.translation: The family sets out what may and may not be done with its things and its information, so acceptable use is stated rather than assumed.

controls.subject: Returning assets when an engagement ends
controls.metaphor: Getting the spare key back when the lodger moves out.
controls.translation: The family collects its property and revokes its access when someone leaves, rather than trusting that unreturned keys will never be used.

controls.subject: Classifying information by how sensitive it is
controls.metaphor: Keeping birth certificates in the safe and takeaway menus in the drawer.
controls.translation: The family sorts its information by how much damage its loss would cause, so that the protection each item gets matches what it is actually worth.

controls.subject: Labelling information so its classification is visible
controls.metaphor: Writing PRIVATE on the folder, so nobody has to open it to find out.
controls.translation: The family marks information clearly enough that anyone handling it can tell how careful to be without having to read it first.

controls.subject: Controlling how information is transferred
controls.metaphor: Posting the passport by tracked delivery rather than dropping it through a letterbox.
controls.translation: The family decides how information may be sent and received, so that something sensitive is not handed over in a way that leaves no trace.

controls.subject: Deciding who may access what, on what basis
controls.metaphor: The teenagers have a front door key; the babysitter does not.
controls.translation: The family decides who may reach what, based on what each person actually needs, rather than giving everyone the same access for convenience.

controls.subject: Managing identities through their whole life
controls.metaphor: Cutting one key per person, with a name on the hook it hangs from.
controls.translation: The family gives each person their own identity rather than a shared one, and manages it from the day it is created to the day it is retired.

controls.subject: Issuing and protecting authentication credentials
controls.metaphor: Not writing the alarm code on a sticky note by the panel.
controls.translation: The family issues the things that prove who someone is carefully, and protects them, because a shared or exposed code protects nobody.

controls.subject: Granting, reviewing, and withdrawing access rights
controls.metaphor: Taking the shed key back once the decking is finished.
controls.translation: The family grants access when it is needed, checks periodically that it is still needed, and takes it back when it is not.

controls.subject: Security in the relationship with each supplier
controls.metaphor: Choosing a builder on more than the quote, because they will have a key.
controls.translation: The family thinks about safety when it brings someone in to do work, because a supplier's access is the family's exposure.

controls.subject: Security terms written into supplier agreements
controls.metaphor: Putting it in the contract rather than the conversation.
controls.translation: The family writes what it expects of a supplier into the agreement, so the obligation survives a change of staff on either side.

controls.subject: Managing risk across the technology supply chain
controls.metaphor: Asking the builder who else will be on site, and who they answer to.
controls.translation: The family looks past its direct supplier to the people that supplier depends on, because a weakness anywhere in that chain still reaches the house.

controls.subject: Monitoring supplier service delivery and change
controls.metaphor: Checking the work as it goes, not only at the final invoice.
controls.translation: The family keeps an eye on how a supplier is actually performing and reassesses when the arrangement changes, rather than trusting the original agreement forever.

controls.subject: Security expectations for cloud services
controls.metaphor: Reading what the storage company is actually responsible for before putting the heirlooms in.
controls.translation: The family sets expectations for the services it rents rather than owns, because handing something to a provider does not hand over the responsibility for it.

controls.subject: Planning and preparing for incident response
controls.metaphor: Agreeing who calls the fire brigade before there is a fire.
controls.translation: The family decides in advance who does what when something goes wrong, so the response is a plan being followed rather than an argument being had.

controls.subject: Assessing events and deciding what is an incident
controls.metaphor: Working out whether the smoke is burnt toast or something worse.
controls.translation: The family assesses what it notices and decides whether it is a real problem, so that small things are not ignored and normal things are not treated as emergencies.

controls.subject: Responding to incidents once declared
controls.metaphor: Getting everyone out first, and worrying about the kitchen afterwards.
controls.translation: Once the family agrees something is genuinely wrong, they act on the plan they made, in the order they agreed mattered most.

controls.subject: Learning from incidents so they do not repeat
controls.metaphor: Moving the pan handles inward after the second burn, not the tenth.
controls.translation: The family works out afterwards what actually went wrong and changes something as a result, so the same incident does not keep happening.

controls.subject: Collecting and preserving evidence
controls.metaphor: Photographing the damage before starting to clear it up.
controls.translation: The family preserves what happened before tidying it away, because the evidence is usually destroyed by the clean-up rather than by the incident.

controls.subject: Keeping security working through disruption
controls.metaphor: Keeping the kettle going on the camping stove when the power is out.
controls.translation: The family works out how it would keep going through a disruption, so that losing one thing does not stop everything.

controls.subject: Recovery expectations built into continuity planning
controls.metaphor: Knowing which room you would make habitable first after a flood.
controls.translation: The family decides in advance what has to come back first and how quickly, so recovery follows a priority rather than whoever shouts loudest.

controls.subject: Identifying legal, regulatory, and contractual obligations
controls.metaphor: Knowing which permits the extension actually needs before building it.
controls.translation: The family works out what the law, the contracts, and the regulators require of it, because an obligation nobody has identified is one nobody is meeting.

controls.subject: Protecting intellectual property rights
controls.metaphor: Buying the software rather than borrowing a copy.
controls.translation: The family respects what belongs to other people, and can show that what it uses it is entitled to use.

controls.subject: Protecting records against loss and falsification
controls.metaphor: Keeping the deeds somewhere they will not be lost, damp, or quietly altered.
controls.translation: The family keeps its important records safe from loss and from tampering, and keeps them for as long as they are actually needed.

controls.subject: Protecting personal data and privacy
controls.metaphor: Not reading someone else's post just because it arrived at your address.
controls.translation: The family treats information about people with the care that person is owed, and meets the specific obligations that attach to it.

controls.subject: Independent review of the security program
controls.metaphor: Asking a friend to walk round the house and say what they would target.
controls.translation: Someone outside the day-to-day running of things reviews whether the arrangements actually work, because the people who built them are the worst placed to judge.

controls.subject: Checking compliance with policies and standards
controls.metaphor: Actually checking the back door is locked, rather than assuming it is.
controls.translation: The family checks that its own rules are being followed in practice, since a rule nobody verifies is a rule nobody has to keep.

controls.subject: Documented operating procedures for security tasks
controls.metaphor: Writing down how the boiler is bled, so it does not live only in one person's head.
controls.translation: The family writes down how its routine tasks are actually done, so the work does not depend on one person remembering or being available.

controls.subject: Screening candidates before they are trusted with access
controls.metaphor: Asking for references before handing over a key to the house.
controls.translation: The family checks who someone is before trusting them with access, in proportion to how much that access could hurt if it were misused.

controls.subject: Security responsibilities set out in employment terms
controls.metaphor: Saying what is expected of the lodger in the tenancy agreement, not on move-in day.
controls.translation: The family writes security expectations into the terms someone agrees to, so the obligation is part of the arrangement rather than a favour.

controls.subject: Security awareness, education, and training
controls.metaphor: Teaching everyone where the stopcock is before the pipe bursts.
controls.translation: The family makes sure everyone knows what is expected of them and how to handle the situations they will actually face, and keeps teaching it.

controls.subject: A disciplinary process for security violations
controls.metaphor: Agreeing in advance what happens if someone keeps leaving the door unlocked.
controls.translation: The family is clear about the consequences of breaking the rules, because a rule with no consequence is advice.

controls.subject: Responsibilities that survive the end of employment
controls.metaphor: Reminding the lodger on their last day that the alarm code stays private.
controls.translation: The family makes clear which obligations continue after someone leaves, because knowing the code does not stop mattering when the tenancy ends.

controls.subject: Confidentiality and non-disclosure agreements
controls.metaphor: Asking the cleaner not to discuss what they see in the house.
controls.translation: The family agrees in writing what must stay private, with anyone who will see things they should not repeat.

controls.subject: Security expectations for remote working
controls.metaphor: Agreeing how the work laptop is looked after when it goes home with someone.
controls.translation: The family sets expectations for working away from the house, because the same information needs looking after wherever it happens to be.

controls.subject: A route for reporting security events
controls.metaphor: Making it easy to say the back gate was open, without anyone getting shouted at.
controls.translation: The family gives everyone a straightforward way to report something that looks wrong, and makes reporting safe enough that people actually use it.

controls.subject: Defining the physical boundary to be protected
controls.metaphor: Deciding where the boundary of the property actually is.
controls.translation: The family works out what it is protecting physically, because you cannot secure a boundary you have never drawn.

controls.subject: Controlling entry at that boundary
controls.metaphor: A front door that is locked, not just closed.
controls.translation: The family controls who can physically get in, so that being inside is something granted rather than something assumed.

controls.subject: Securing offices, rooms, and facilities
controls.metaphor: The study door has a lock; the hallway does not need one.
controls.translation: The family gives more protection to the rooms that hold what matters, rather than treating every space the same.

controls.subject: Monitoring physical premises
controls.metaphor: A light that comes on when someone walks up the drive.
controls.translation: The family keeps an eye on the premises, so that someone being where they should not be is noticed rather than discovered later.

controls.subject: Protecting against physical and environmental threats
controls.metaphor: Moving the boxes off the cellar floor before the wet season.
controls.translation: The family protects what it owns from flood, fire, heat, and the other things the environment does regardless of anyone's intent.

controls.subject: Working securely in secure areas
controls.metaphor: Not leaving the safe open while you go and answer the door.
controls.translation: The family behaves differently in the rooms that hold sensitive things, because the protection is only as good as the habits inside it.

controls.subject: Clear desk and clear screen expectations
controls.metaphor: Clearing the paperwork off the kitchen table before the party.
controls.translation: The family puts sensitive things away when they walk off, and locks the screen, so what is left out is not what matters.

controls.subject: Siting and protecting equipment
controls.metaphor: Not putting the router on the windowsill by the front path.
controls.translation: The family thinks about where equipment sits, so that important things are not the easiest ones to reach or damage.

controls.subject: Protecting assets taken off the premises
controls.metaphor: The laptop is more at risk in the café than in the study.
controls.translation: The family gives extra care to things taken away from the house, because the protections at home do not travel with them.

controls.subject: Managing storage media through their life
controls.metaphor: Knowing where the old photo albums and the backup drive actually are.
controls.translation: The family looks after the things that hold its information, from the day they arrive to the day they are destroyed.

controls.subject: Protecting supporting utilities such as power
controls.metaphor: Keeping a torch and candles for when the power goes.
controls.translation: The family protects the services everything else depends on, because losing power or water stops things no lock can keep running.

controls.subject: Protecting cabling from interception and damage
controls.metaphor: Running the cable under the floor rather than across the hallway.
controls.translation: The family protects the wiring that carries its power and data, since a cable anyone can reach is a cable anyone can cut or tap.

controls.subject: Maintaining equipment so it stays reliable
controls.metaphor: Servicing the boiler before winter rather than after it fails.
controls.translation: The family maintains its equipment so that it keeps working, because most outages start as maintenance nobody got around to.

controls.subject: Secure disposal or reuse of equipment
controls.metaphor: Wiping the old phone before giving it to a cousin.
controls.translation: The family makes sure nothing readable is left on equipment before it is passed on, sold, or thrown away.

controls.subject: Protecting the endpoints people work from
controls.metaphor: Locking the laptop the same way you lock the front door.
controls.translation: The family protects the devices people actually work from, because that is where most trouble starts rather than at the perimeter.

controls.subject: Restricting and managing privileged access
controls.metaphor: Only one person has the key to the medicine cabinet, and they do not carry it everywhere.
controls.translation: The family keeps the powerful access separate and limited, and does not use it for everyday tasks where it is not needed.

controls.subject: Restricting access to information itself
controls.metaphor: The diary is in the drawer, and not everyone opens that drawer.
controls.translation: The family restricts who can reach the information itself, not only who can get through the front door.

controls.subject: Controlling access to source code
controls.metaphor: The recipe book the business depends on is not left on the counter.
controls.translation: The family controls who can see and change the instructions its work is built from, since those are worth more than any single dish.

controls.subject: Authenticating securely before access is granted
controls.metaphor: Recognising the voice through the door before opening it.
controls.translation: The family checks who someone actually is before letting them in, in a way that is hard to fake.

controls.subject: Managing capacity so systems stay available
controls.metaphor: Noticing the freezer is nearly full before the weekly shop.
controls.translation: The family watches whether it is running out of room or capacity, so that things fail on a plan rather than by surprise.

controls.subject: Defending against malware
controls.metaphor: Wiping your feet, and keeping the mousetraps set.
controls.translation: The family defends against the things that get in and spread, and keeps those defences current rather than installed once.

controls.subject: Managing technical vulnerabilities
controls.metaphor: Fixing the loose window latch once you know about it.
controls.translation: The family finds out where the weaknesses are and fixes them on a timescale that matches how bad they would be.

controls.subject: Managing configuration and preventing drift
controls.metaphor: Every door in the house is fitted the same way, and stays that way.
controls.translation: The family sets things up to a known standard and notices when something drifts away from it, rather than discovering the difference during a break-in.

controls.subject: Deleting information when it is no longer needed
controls.metaphor: Shredding the old bank statements instead of keeping every one forever.
controls.translation: The family gets rid of information once it is genuinely no longer needed, because what is not held cannot be lost.

controls.subject: Masking data so exposure is limited
controls.metaphor: Reading out only the last four digits of the card number.
controls.translation: The family shows only as much of something sensitive as the task actually requires, and hides the rest.

controls.subject: Preventing data from leaking out
controls.metaphor: Noticing that the box of documents is being carried out to the car.
controls.translation: The family watches for its information leaving by routes it did not intend, rather than only guarding the way in.

controls.subject: Backing up information and proving it restores
controls.metaphor: Keeping copies of the photos somewhere the same fire cannot reach.
controls.translation: The family keeps copies of what matters, somewhere separate, and checks that the copies actually work before it needs them.

controls.subject: Building redundancy into information processing
controls.metaphor: A second kettle, so a broken one does not end tea.
controls.translation: The family builds in enough spare capacity that the failure of one thing does not stop what depends on it.

controls.subject: Logging what happens on systems
controls.metaphor: A visitors' book by the door that people actually sign.
controls.translation: The family keeps a record of what happened and when, because you cannot investigate what nobody wrote down.

controls.subject: Monitoring for activity that should not be there
controls.metaphor: Noticing the pantry light is on at three in the morning.
controls.translation: The family watches for activity that does not fit the normal pattern, since the record is only useful if somebody reads it.

controls.subject: Synchronizing clocks so events can be correlated
controls.metaphor: Setting every clock in the house to the same time.
controls.translation: The family keeps its clocks in step, so that piecing together the order of events afterwards is possible at all.

controls.subject: Restricting use of privileged utility programs
controls.metaphor: The crowbar lives in the locked shed, not by the back door.
controls.translation: The family restricts the tools that can bypass its own protections, because a tool that overrides a lock is as good as a key.

controls.subject: Controlling software installed on operational systems
controls.metaphor: Deciding what gets installed in the house, rather than whatever anyone brings home.
controls.translation: The family controls what software runs on the systems it depends on, so the working parts of the house are ones it chose.

controls.subject: Securing networks and the services on them
controls.metaphor: The wiring in the walls is as much part of the house as the doors.
controls.translation: The family protects the networks everything runs over, since anything that reaches the wiring reaches everything on it.

controls.subject: Securing individual network services
controls.metaphor: The outside tap is turned off at the stopcock in winter.
controls.translation: The family secures each service it offers or uses individually, rather than assuming the network around it is enough.

controls.subject: Segregating networks from one another
controls.metaphor: A door between the garage and the house, so a fire in one is not a fire in both.
controls.translation: The family separates parts of its network, so trouble that gets into one area does not automatically reach the rest.

controls.subject: Filtering access to external web content
controls.metaphor: Not clicking every link that arrives, and teaching the children the same.
controls.translation: The family filters what it reaches out to on the web, because a lot of trouble arrives by invitation rather than by force.

controls.subject: Using cryptography and managing keys
controls.metaphor: A diary with a lock, and keeping the little key somewhere sensible.
controls.translation: The family scrambles what is sensitive so it cannot simply be read, and looks after the keys as carefully as the contents.

controls.subject: Security built into the development lifecycle
controls.metaphor: Designing the extension for safety, rather than adding bolts once it is up.
controls.translation: The family builds safety into how it makes things from the beginning, because it is far cheaper than adding it afterwards.

controls.subject: Security requirements defined for applications
controls.metaphor: Agreeing the extension needs a fire door before drawing the plans.
controls.translation: The family decides what protections something must have before it is built, rather than discovering the requirement at inspection.

controls.subject: Secure architecture and engineering principles
controls.metaphor: Building on foundations that are known to work, not improvised each time.
controls.translation: The family follows established principles when it designs something, so the safety does not depend on whoever happened to build it.

controls.subject: Writing code securely
controls.metaphor: Measuring twice, because the cut is what everyone else builds on.
controls.translation: The family writes carefully, because a mistake made early is inherited by everything built on top of it.

controls.subject: Security testing during development and acceptance
controls.metaphor: Checking the shelf holds weight before putting the good china on it.
controls.translation: The family tests things before relying on them, and tests for the ways they might fail rather than only that they work.

controls.subject: Managing security when development is outsourced
controls.metaphor: Checking the work of the contractor who built the extension.
controls.translation: The family holds work done by others to the same standard as its own, because who built it does not change who lives with it.

controls.subject: Separating development, test, and production
controls.metaphor: Not testing the new recipe on the dinner guests.
controls.translation: The family keeps where it experiments separate from where it lives, so a mistake in one does not land in the other.

controls.subject: Managing change to systems and software
controls.metaphor: Telling the household before moving the fuse box.
controls.translation: The family manages changes deliberately, so that things break because of decisions rather than surprises.

controls.subject: Protecting information used for testing
controls.metaphor: Practising with an old photo rather than the wedding album.
controls.translation: The family uses stand-in information when testing, so a rehearsal cannot expose the real thing.

controls.subject: Protecting systems during audit activity
controls.metaphor: Having the surveyor visit at a time that does not flood the kitchen.
controls.translation: The family plans checks on its systems so the checking itself does not cause the disruption it was meant to prevent.
